subject: Cuban boa
title: Snakes Formed a Wall in a Cave and Caught Bats 30 Times in 30 Tries

scenes.text: Snakes almost always hunt alone. In one Cuban cave, they team up.
Every dusk, hundreds of fruit bats fly out through one narrow tunnel.
Cuban boas hang from its ceiling and snatch them right out of the air.
A lone boa caught a bat in one of three tries, after about nineteen minutes.
But latecomers hang beside the boas already there, forming a living fence across the tunnel.
With two or three snakes, all thirty attempts worked. Three boas needed under seven minutes.

description:
Cuban boas hang from the ceiling of a cave passage and grab Jamaican fruit bats in mid-air as they fly out.
In a 2017 study in Animal Behavior and Cognition, boas arriving later chose spots next to boas already hunting, forming a fence across the passage: group hunts succeeded 30 times out of 30, solo hunts once in three, and capture time fell from about 19 minutes for one boa to 6.7 minutes for three.
It was the first direct test of coordinated hunting in a reptile.
Would you walk through that cave at dusk?
first_comment: Only a handful of the roughly 3,650 snake species have ever been seen hunting in groups. Which animal would you least want hunting in a pack?
